constants.cheap_path: mandatory: taken when checkpoint[X.height] = keccak256(X), after the checks of steps 1–6; steps 9–12 (the signature check and the SccpCertificate event) are skipped

conventions: each scenario deploys a fresh destination from `deployment` (its `initial_state`), then runs `steps` in order; a step is (state, call, now_ms) → (state_after, expected.outcome, expected.events). `now_ms` is the destination clock: block.timestamp (EVM) or now() (TON) in whole seconds, times 1000, so every `now_ms` is a multiple of 1000; within a scenario `now_ms` never decreases from one step to the next (equal values are calls in the same block or second). Taira-side times (`X.timestamp_ms`, `untilMs`, payload deadlines, fast-pause expiries) are milliseconds and may be sub-second, so a time boundary is probed with the nearest whole-second clock values on both sides. `ok` is success (a latch or a lost Live inside submitCheckpoints is success with `stopped`); any other outcome is the §5.2.2 error and the call changes nothing. Certificates are pooled under `certificates` and referenced by id; an SccpCertificate event names the pooled certificate whose QC_FIXED, header and signature it publishes; `committees` resolve `signed_by` and TON `next_keys`. A step names its call as its flavor does: the EVM entry point, or the TON message of §5.3.2 (`ton_call_names`). An EVM scenario runs on ethereum-mainnet with the destination word word(0x22…22) and 20-byte recipients. A TON scenario runs on ton-mainnet: Taira's leaves use lane_bytes(sora-taira, ton-mainnet), recipients are 36-byte accounts of workchain 0, and the destination word is the harness-installed minter account id 0x35…35. Events list the SCCP events only (the ERC-20 Transfer of a mint is implied). `state_after.checkpoints` is a set (sorted by height for readability). `ton_replayable` marks EVM scenarios that a TON harness replays as one sccp_checkpoint message per step (using each certificate's `ton` form and `ton_next_keys`) with identical outcomes and state; such a row contains checkpoint submissions only, which do not depend on the profile. `init_bounds` lists the deployment bound on the pinned untilMs: the constructor (EVM) or sccp_init (TON) at `now_ms` accepts `until_ms` iff now_ms < until_ms ≤ now_ms + max_validity_ms + max_init_slack_ms, and answers BadConfig otherwise

error_choices.check_order: submitCheckpoints checks TooManyCertificates, then an empty batch (NothingToDo), then Live, then each certificate; the inline entry points obtain X first (VerifyCertificate with V1–V3 → LatchRequired) and check Live after it, in the §5.1.5 step order; the checkpoint entry points check the X length (BadHeader), the stored id (UnknownCheckpoint), X1–X7 with ACTIVE (BadHeader), Live, and then that X is of the current generation or the handoff that installed it (CommitteeNotAccepted); VerifyCertificate checks the key and signature encodings of step 6, including the identity signature on both flavors, before the cheap path of step 8; on EVM step 10 reports apk = O (BadCommittee) before step 11 reads σ as a point; a TON finalize or void checks the payload and its recipient (BadPayload, BadRecipient) before it obtains X (§5.3.4), while EVM checks them after X, Live, the pause and the block reference; on both flavors the deadline is checked before the leaf path, a consumed nonce (AlreadyConsumed) before the supply cap, the §3.4 constraints (BadControl) before the control nonce (StaleControl), and the nonce argument of voidExpired (BadNonce) before the consumed set; voidFrozen checks the range before Frozen
error_choices.note: these are the error names and the check order of specs/sccp.md §5.1.2, §5.1.3 and §5.1.8, repeated here so that every harness keys on one table

error_codes.note: §5.2.2: the EVM error name and its TON exit code (null: EVM only); scenario outcomes use the names

generator: two generators write this file byte for byte: the independent Python reference (python3 scripts/sccp_reference/generate.py --write, Python 3.10+) and the Rust reference (cargo test -p iroha_sccp --test v1_reference_finality --test v1_reference_transitions --test v1_reference_control -- --ignored regenerate)
model_scope: TON finalize and void bucket round trips and bounce recovery (§5.3.4) are covered by the Acton contract harness. These atomic-model ton_* scenarios contain only steps the minter decides alone: checkpoints, controls, and finalize, void and voidFrozen steps that it refuses before any bucket message

The Acton harness installs the minter at account id 0x35…35 in workchain 0. The applied controls of ton_checkpoint_use_after_rotation and ton_same_height_block_ref_with_history commit to that destination word in their leaves

The Acton harness and finality_v1.json pin BadSignature when BLS_FASTAGGREGATEVERIFY refuses a signer key that is no canonical point, is the identity or lies outside G1 (error_choices.ton_signer_key_refused_by_the_opcode)

scenarios.description: the state a constructor (EVM) or sccp_init (TON) leaves: cur from the pin, high = start − 1
scenarios.name: initial_pin

scenarios.description: a non-rotation CUR certificate records its checkpoint and raises high; untilMs is unchanged; a CUR certificate below high records a checkpoint without moving high; a replay changes nothing
scenarios.name: checkpoint_raises_high

scenarios.description: a ROTATION certificate of the current generation installs generation 6 with untilMs = t_eff(X) + validity_ms; the successor's certificates are then CUR
scenarios.name: rotation_key_change

scenarios.description: a heartbeat (next_committee_root = committee_root) installs generation 6 with the same keys and a fresh deadline
scenarios.name: heartbeat_rotation

scenarios.description: a rotation with validity_ms = 3 d gives the successor a deadline earlier than its predecessor's
scenarios.name: rotation_lowered_validity

scenarios.description: a destination lagging past the successor's deadline applies the rotation, becomes Frozen and stops processing; then voids drain it
scenarios.name: rotation_successor_already_expired

scenarios.description: 16 rotations K0 → K16 in one submitCheckpoints call; 17 certificates revert TooManyCertificates
scenarios.name: sixteen_batched_rotations

scenarios.description: K → K′ → K: generation 7 has K's root again; a genuine certificate of generation 5 (same root) is refused
scenarios.name: k_kprime_k

scenarios.description: a future-dated non-rotation certificate is accepted but never extends untilMs; replays change nothing; after the pin's deadline it is refused and voidFrozen opens
scenarios.name: future_dated_replay_no_extension

scenarios.description: a departed quorum of generation 5 signs heights above its genuine end: accepted (bounded); the genuine handoff then trips V3 and latches; voidFrozen opens
scenarios.name: forged_heights_then_genuine_handoff_latches

scenarios.description: after generations 6 and 7 are installed, genuine and forged certificates of generations 5 and 6 (any height, ROTATION or not) are refused with no state change
scenarios.name: old_generations_refused

scenarios.description: V1: a second, different X at a recorded height signed by cur latches with reason 1
scenarios.name: v1_two_x_at_one_height

scenarios.description: the same X with a different result_body (signed) records nothing and does not latch
scenarios.name: v1_neighbour_same_x_other_result_body

scenarios.description: V2: a CUR certificate below cur.start latches with reason 2
scenarios.name: v2_below_start

scenarios.description: a CUR certificate at exactly cur.start is accepted
scenarios.name: v2_neighbour_at_start

scenarios.description: V3: a ROTATION certificate below cur.high latches with reason 3
scenarios.name: v3_rotation_below_high

scenarios.description: the handoff used inline first (finalizeFromTaira records it and raises high to its height without installing), then submitted: ROTATION at height = high installs
scenarios.name: v3_neighbour_rotation_at_high

scenarios.description: at untilMs the destination is still Live; at the next clock value (one second later) submitCheckpoints and finalize are refused, voidFrozen voids, a second voidFrozen of the same nonce reverts
scenarios.name: expiry_then_refusal_then_void_frozen

scenarios.description: [ok, V2 violation, ok]: the first is applied, the latch persists and the third is not processed
scenarios.name: latch_inside_batch

scenarios.description: an inline use of a violating certificate reverts LatchRequired; the relayer resubmits it through submitCheckpoints, which latches
scenarios.name: inline_v3_latch_required_then_submit_latches

scenarios.description: a rotation X timed 10 d ahead installs untilMs = now + validity_ms (t_eff = min(X.timestamp_ms, now))
scenarios.name: future_dated_rotation_t_eff

scenarios.description: inline and checkpoint finalization, a history proof, replay, deadline, recipient, supply-cap and proof failures, and voidExpired
scenarios.name: finalize_proofs_cap_and_voids

scenarios.description: TON: a key-changing rotation needs next_keys hashing to X.next_committee_root (missing or wrong → BadCommittee); a heartbeat keeps the stored keys without next_keys
scenarios.name: ton_rotation_next_keys

scenarios.description: TON keeps three checkpoints: a higher height evicts the lowest, a height at or below the lowest is not stored, conflicts are detected only for retained entries, an evicted checkpoint is unknown
scenarios.name: ton_checkpoint_eviction

scenarios.description: a rotation X with a sub-second timestamp_ms installs the sub-second untilMs = t_eff(X) + validity_ms; the whole-second destination clock is Live at the last second at or below untilMs and Frozen at the next one, which is untilMs + 1 ms
scenarios.name: rotation_sub_second_deadline

scenarios.description: the cheap path is mandatory and observable: a certificate of X whose signature covers another instance is refused while X is not stored and accepted without a signature check once it is (nothing changes, so NothingToDo); the identity signature is refused before the cheap path
scenarios.name: cheap_path_identity_signature

scenarios.description: the cheap path is mandatory and observable: a certificate of X whose signature covers another instance is refused while X is not stored and accepted without a signature check once it is (nothing changes, so NothingToDo); the identity signature is refused before the cheap path
scenarios.name: ton_cheap_path_identity_signature

scenarios.description: a whole-second deadline_ms: at it a finalization is accepted and a void is early, one second later the finalization is late and the void is accepted; a deadline_ms ending in 999 ms: the same pairs at the last clock value below it (999 ms earlier) and at the next one (1 ms later)
scenarios.name: transfer_deadline_boundaries

scenarios.description: a stored checkpoint is usable while its header is of the current generation (U1) or is the handoff that installed it (U2): after the handoff of generation 5 is installed, a non-handoff checkpoint of generation 5 is refused for finalize, control and void while the handoff checkpoint proves the same leaves through its history root; after generation 7 is installed the handoff of generation 5 and every non-handoff checkpoint of generations 5 and 6 are refused, and the handoff of generation 6 is usable
scenarios.name: checkpoint_use_after_rotation

scenarios.description: TON: after the handoff of generation 5 is installed its non-handoff checkpoint is refused and the handoff checkpoint applies the control through its history root; after generation 7 is installed the handoff of generation 5 is refused and the handoff of generation 6 is usable
scenarios.name: ton_checkpoint_use_after_rotation

scenarios.description: voidFrozen on a Live destination: a range failure is reported before NotFrozen (count 0, a count above the bound, a range past 2^64 and, on TON, a range that crosses a 512-nonce bucket); a valid range is NotFrozen
scenarios.name: void_frozen_range_before_frozen

scenarios.description: voidFrozen on a Live destination: a range failure is reported before NotFrozen (count 0, a count above the bound, a range past 2^64 and, on TON, a range that crosses a 512-nonce bucket); a valid range is NotFrozen
scenarios.name: ton_void_frozen_range_before_frozen

scenarios.description: two faults in one call: a payload of another revision, or one that pays the contract itself, under a checkpoint that is not stored (EVM reports the checkpoint, the TON minter the payload); a finalization after the deadline with a wrong leaf path (the deadline is reported); a void with a wrong nonce argument under a checkpoint that is not stored
scenarios.name: finalize_two_faults

scenarios.description: two faults in one call: a payload of another revision, or one that pays the contract itself, under a checkpoint that is not stored (EVM reports the checkpoint, the TON minter the payload); a finalization after the deadline with a wrong leaf path (the deadline is reported); a void with a wrong nonce argument under a checkpoint that is not stored
scenarios.name: ton_finalize_two_faults

scenarios.description: a control leaf with track 3 and a nonce below the stored one is BadControl, not StaleControl; a finalization of a consumed nonce at a full supply cap is AlreadyConsumed, not SupplyCapExceeded; a voidExpired of a consumed payload with a wrong nonce argument is BadNonce, not AlreadyConsumed
scenarios.name: check_order_two_faults

scenarios.description: the encodings of step 6 are checked before the cheap path: once X is stored, the same certificate with signerYs[0] + p, with signerYs[0] = p − y (the other sign) or with the first σ limb + p is refused, and the unchanged certificate is accepted without a signature check (NothingToDo)
scenarios.name: cheap_path_checks_encodings

scenarios.description: a reference to the certified block itself carries no history proof: with historyIndex 1, or with a historyPath of one sibling, it is BadProof for an inline finalization and, under the stored checkpoint, for a control, a finalization and a void; the unchanged proofs are accepted (in the TON row the control only: a mint and a void end in the bucket)
scenarios.name: same_height_block_ref_with_history

scenarios.description: a reference to the certified block itself carries no history proof: with historyIndex 1, or with a historyPath of one sibling, it is BadProof for an inline finalization and, under the stored checkpoint, for a control, a finalization and a void; the unchanged proofs are accepted (in the TON row the control only: a mint and a void end in the bucket)
scenarios.name: ton_same_height_block_ref_with_history

scenarios.description: an inline entry point obtains X before it checks Live: on a destination whose generation has expired, a certificate whose signature covers another instance is BadSignature for a finalization, a control and a void, and the genuine certificate of the current generation is CommitteeNotAccepted; neither stores a checkpoint
scenarios.name: inline_calls_after_expiry

scenarios.description: an inline entry point obtains X before it checks Live: on a destination whose generation has expired, a certificate whose signature covers another instance is BadSignature for a finalization, a control and a void, and the genuine certificate of the current generation is CommitteeNotAccepted; neither stores a checkpoint
scenarios.name: ton_inline_calls_after_expiry
